claim: The SQS documentation history row of July 24, 2024 says that SQS no longer requires the kms:Decrypt permission for the SendMessage API and that customers only need kms:GenerateDataKey on the KMS key (but still need kms:Decrypt to call ReceiveMessage). The current key-management page still says that the producer must have the kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey permissions for the KMS key.

values.display: still need kms:Decrypt permission to call ReceiveMessage
the producer must have the kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey permissions

note: AWS pages disagree: the 2024 history row versus the current producer section of sqs-key-management. Teach: grant a producer both kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt (see sqs-faq-sse-producer-needs-generatedatakey-and-decrypt).

evidence.quote: | [AWSkms:Decrypt](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-key-management.html#compatibility-with-aws-services) | Amazon SQS no longer requires the `kms:Decrypt` permission for the `SendMessage` API. Customers now only need the `kms:GenerateDataKey` permission on the KMS key used to encrypt the queue, but still need `kms:Decrypt` permission to call `ReceiveMessage`. | July 24, 2024 |

When the data key reuse period expires, the producer's next call to SendMessage or SendMessageBatch also triggers calls to kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey. The call to kms:Decrypt is to verify the integrity of the new data key before using it. Therefore, the producer must have the kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey permissions for the KMS key.
